If you're ready to be part of our legacy of hope and innovation, we encourage you to take the first step and explore our current job openings. Your best is waiting to be discovered.

 
Day - 08 Hour (United States of America)

**This is a Stanford Health Care job.** 
 
**A Brief Overview** 
The Director of Supply Chain Operational Excellence is a senior leadership role driving enterprise‑wide efficiency, innovation, and transformation across a Gartner top‑2 ranked healthcare supply chain. With system‑wide influence and a seat at the leadership table, this role partners closely with the Chief Supply Chain Officer and Vice President of Strategic Initiatives to turn strategy into measurable results. The ideal candidate combines healthcare supply chain expertise with strong program management skills and a passion for developing people, leading change, and delivering measurable, enterprise‑wide impact. 
 
**Locations** 
Stanford Health Care 
 
**What you will do**

* Maintain continuous alignment with defined organizational and departmental strategic business objectives in conjunction with leadership.
* Direct and ensure the efficient operation of day-to-day activities of the team and ensure competency of all staff.
* Supports and partners on Change Management, Training and Communications activities as needed for effective performance improvement and project management.
* Act in an advisory capacity to all Supply Chain divisions, programs, staff and leaders.
* Provide expertise, guidance and training on Performance Improvement and Project Management best practices.
* Apply LEAN/Six Sigma principles and methods to identify waste reduction and performance optimization opportunities across Supply Chain operations.
* Implement, oversee and continuously improve Supply Chain systems, processes and standard work to drive the efficient management of operations across Logistics, Sourcing, Procurement, Business Office, Resiliency, Sustainability, Data Management and other functions.
* Build, develop and grow business relationships with Supply Chain’s key stakeholders and partners including but not limited to the Interventional Platform, A/P, Pharmacy, and IT.
* Lead cross-departmental initiatives, establishing strong governance, communication, and accountability to deliver progress measurable through mutually agreed KPIs.
* Align and collaborate with the enterprise Performance Improvement team and Stanford Operating System (SOS).
* Lead the implementation of programs and/or projects as assigned by the Administrative Director.

**Education Qualifications**

* Requires a Bachelor’s degree in a work-related discipline/field from an accredited college or university.
* Relevant experience in lieu of degree may be considered. Relevant experience in lieu of degree is in addition to the experience requirements for this position.

**Experience Qualifications**

* Seven (7) years of progressively responsible and directly related work experience.

**Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

* Must have strong leadership and interpersonal skills and be effective at people management including the ability to delegate assignments and share decision-making with team members and direct reports as appropriate.
* Excellent communication skills including the ability to present, and to write in a clear and understandable manner.
* Ability to understand complex verbal or written instructions and translate to action to deliver quantitative and qualitative results.
* Must be well organized and systematic, and able to design, implement and maintain standard work processes.
* Knowledge of project management methodologies to lead complex project teams and large scope projects, including managing resources (people, costs, time).
* Familiar with and able to apply Lean Six Sigma concepts and techniques including value stream mapping, kaizen, Five Whys, VoC, RCA etc. for structured process improvement.
* Demonstrated expertise in leading change management initiatives within Agile delivery environments.
* Ability to multi-task and handle multiple priorities while managing aggressive deadlines. Knowledge of Supply Chain functions, practices, and operational challenges.
* Understanding of healthcare and clinical concepts.

**Licenses and Certifications**

* Lean Six Sigma Certification preferred .
* PMP - Project Mgmt Professional preferred .
* CMRP (Certified Materials & Resource Professionals) preferred.

**Physical Demands and Work Conditions** 
**Blood Borne Pathogens**

* Category II - Tasks that involve NO exposure to blood, body fluids or tissues, but employment may require performing unplanned Category I tasks

**These principles apply to ALL employees:** 
 
**SHC Commitment to Providing an Exceptional Patient & Family Experience** 
 
*Stanford Health Care sets a high standard for delivering value and an exceptional experience for our patients and families. Candidates for employment and existing employees must adopt and execute C-I-CARE standards for all of patients, families and towards each other. C-I-CARE is the foundation of Stanford’s patient-experience and represents a framework for patient-centered interactions. Simply put, we do what it takes to enable and empower patients and families to focus on health, healing and recovery.* 
 
*You will do this by executing against our three experience pillars, from the patient and family’s perspective:*

* Know Me: Anticipate my needs and status to deliver effective care
* Show Me the Way: Guide and prompt my actions to arrive at better outcomes and better health
* Coordinate for Me: Own the complexity of my care through coordination

**Equal Opportunity Employer Stanford Health Care (SHC) strongly values diversity and is committed to equal opportunity and non-discrimination in****all of****its policies and practices, including the area of employment. Accordingly, SHC does not discriminate against any person on the basis of race, color, sex, sexual orientation or gender identity and/or expression, religion, age, national or ethnic origin, political beliefs, marital status, medical condition, genetic information, veteran status, or disability, or the perception of any of the above. People of all genders, members of all racial and ethnic groups, people with disabilities, and veterans are encouraged to apply. Qualified applicants with criminal convictions will be considered after an individualized assessment of the conviction and the job requirements.**

Base Pay Scale: Generally starting at $81.59 - $108.12 per hour

The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be set based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to, internal equity, experience, education, specialty and training. This pay scale is not a promise of a particular wage.

card.title: EXPERIENCED PLANT MANAGER
card.description:
Kingspan Insulated Panels North America, a division of the Kingspan Group plc headquartered in Ireland, is a global and trusted leader in the design, manufacturing, and supply of high-performance sustainable building products and solutions for the construction industry. As the most energy-efficient, cost-effective building envelope solutions, insulated metal panels are at the forefront of sustainability. We serve the architectural, commercial/industrial, cold storage and food processing markets, and are committed to delivering the most advanced building products on the market.

Learn about our Planet Passionate initiatives: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EEeIS55WMOk (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EEeIS55WMOk)

At Kingspan, our future success is based on the quality of our people, who's expertise and motivation have helped ensure that we remain at the forefront of the construction materials manufacturing industry. In joining Kingspan you become an important part of a growing organization with a reputation for innovative design and use of technology, technical expertise, product quality, service excellence, and dedication to sustainability.

***Ready to be part of our team?***

***We are looking for an Experienced Plant Manager for our Columbus, OH plant!***

* **Sponsorship is not available for this position.**

**Summary:** The Plant Manager is the senior site leader with full accountability for overall plant performance, overseeing all operations across the entire site, including continuous panel line manufacturing and ancillary processes. This role is responsible for aligning people, processes, and strategy to ensure the site produces high-quality products at standard manufacturing costs in a safe, efficient, and profitable manner.

Success is achieved through the direct leadership and development of subordinate managers and supervisors, while building a strong, engaged organization capable of delivering reliable operational and business results.

**Essential Duties**

**Operational Performance & KPI Accountability**

* Own and drive plant performance against key metrics, including safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, productivity, and employee engagement.
* Translate corporate and regional objectives into clear plant-level goals, priorities, and operating plans.
* Ensure disciplined execution of daily management systems, standard work, and KPI reviews.
* Hold leaders and teams accountable for results while removing barriers and providing necessary resources.
* Ensure customer requirements are met through effective production planning, quality control, and on-time delivery.

**Organizational Leadership & People Development**

* Provide visible, values-based leadership that sets clear expectations for behavior, performance, and accountability across all levels of the plant.
* Lead, coach, and develop managers and supervisors, ensuring they are equipped to lead teams, solve problems, and deliver results through others.
* Build a high performing leadership team through effective hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, and succession planning.
* Foster an inclusive, respectful, and engaged workplace culture where safety, quality, and continuous improvement are shared responsibilities.
* Communicate effectively and consistently with employees, reinforcing vision, priorities, and alignment to company objectives.
* Partner with Human Resources to address employee relations matters, labor strategy (where applicable), and workforce planning.

**Safety, Quality & Compliance Leadership**

* Champion a proactive safety culture by modeling safe behaviors, enforcing standards, leading incident investigations, and driving corrective actions.
* Ensure compliance with all regulatory, environmental, safety, and labor requirements.
* Maintain adherence to quality standards and lead continuous improvement efforts to reduce defects and variability.
* Act as the site authority for audits, inspections, and regulatory interactions.

**Continuous Improvement & Change Leadership**

* Lead lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives that improve performance and build organizational capability.
* Drive root-cause problem solving and data-driven decision making.
* Lead change initiatives effectively by engaging stakeholders, communicating clearly, and sustaining improvements over time.
* Balance short-term operational execution with long-term capability and talent development.

**Financial & Strategic Stewardship**

* Maintain full accountability for plant financial performance, including labor, operating costs, and capital investments.
* Participate in budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning. • Identify and mitigate operational and business risks to ensure continuity and stability.
* Evaluate and prepare CAPEX recommendations.
* Serve as the primary site representative to corporate partners, customers, and external stakeholders.

**General Responsibilities**

* Maintain accurate records and reporting across all operational areas.
* Participate in meetings, training, and development activities as required.
* Follow the Group Code of Conduct and Group Compliance.
* Follow Compliance requirements per “KNA-SOP-1705 Compliance Roles and Responsibilities.”
* Performs all other duties as assigned.

**Education/Experience:**

* Formal education is preferably a bachelor’s degree or above.
* 10 years of manufacturing experience, ideally in a continuous product environment.
* Knowledge and practice of modern manufacturing techniques.
* Knowledge of labor laws.
* Knowledge of the construction industry.
* Know the operation of the panel producing equipment and accessory equipment.
* Ability to calculate figures/amounts.
* Good oral and written communication skills.
* Ability to train and instruct employees.
* Good analytical problem-solving skills.
* Strong Microsoft Word and Excel skills.
* Proven track record of lean manufacturing experience.
* Must be highly proficient in all Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and Outlook.

**Personal Attributes**

The successful candidate will exhibit the following attributes:

**Senior Site Leadership**

* Serves as the visible, accountable plant leader, shaping performance, culture, and behavior.
* Builds long-term organizational capability while balancing operational urgency with people and succession needs.

**People-Centered, Results-Driven**

* Delivers results through strong managers and supervisors, not direct control.
* Sets clear expectations, fosters accountability and trust, and coaches leaders to manage performance fairly and effectively.

**Operational & Strategic Focus**

* Aligns KPIs and execution with business objectives, customer commitments, and financial results.
* Uses data, standard work, and problem-solving while maintaining both short-term execution and long-term excellence.

**Comfort with Complexity**

* Makes sound decisions in dynamic, ambiguous environments with competing priorities.
* Leads calmly and decisively through disruptions, pressure, and change.

**Influence-Based Leadership**

* Is visible on the factory floor, approachable, and accessible to team members, fostering open dialogue and trust.
* Builds alignment through credibility and relationships rather than authority.
* Effectively influences cross-functional partners and gains buy-in at all organizational levels.

**Change & Continuous Improvement**

* Champions continuous improvement as a performance system and leadership mindset.
* Engages teams in change and sustains gains through embedded leadership routines.

**Safety, Values & Integrity**

* Models personal accountability for safety, quality, and ethical behavior.
* Treats safety, respect for people, and values as non-negotiable standards.

**Executive Presence**

* Communicates clearly and confidently across all levels.
* Represents the site professionally with corporate leaders, customers, and external stakeholders.

**Physical Demands:** The physical demands described here represent those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform key responsibilities.

**Body Movement & Posture:** Standing or walking for extended periods, frequent bending, stooping, crouching, or kneeling, climbing stairs or ladders, crawling, or working in confined spaces.

**Manual Dexterity & Handling:** Using hands and fingers to grasp, manipulate, or assemble objects, operating machinery or tools with precision, repetitive motion tasks (e.g., packaging, sorting).

**Strength & Lifting:** Lifting and carrying materials (often 25–50 lbs.). Pushing or pulling carts, pallets, or equipment. Adjusting body movements to match the pace of moving objects.

**Sensory Requirements:** Near and far visual acuity for spotting defects or reading gauges. Hearing alarms, instructions, or machinery sounds. Peripheral vision for monitoring surroundings.

**Cognitive & Environmental Factors:** Maintaining focus in noisy or fast-paced environments. Performing tasks independently or in teams. Exposure to heat, cold, dust, or chemicals, depending on the facility.

We offer a comprehensive benefits package including 401k with company match, Medical, Dental, Vision, Identity Theft Protection, Critical Illness, Accident, Hospital Indemnity, Pregnancy and Parental Leave, Fitness Reimbursement, Educational Assistance, Life, AD&D, Short- and Long-Term Disability, and Life Assistance Program.

Kingspan is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any factor, including veteran status and disability status, protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

Equal Opportunity Employer 
This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights (https://www.eeoc.gov/poster) notice from the Department of Labor.

card.title: Plant Manager
card.description:
This position will oversee production to enable plant productivity and maintenance and the delivery of quality products to customers in an efficient manner, performs various manual tasks in the pits as required. Production activities and coordinates projects. Maintains quality control and ensures the project is going smoothly and according to schedule.

**Essentials Functions**

* Full and complete working knowledge and understanding of all equipment.
* Promotes and supports safety culture and ensures compliance with safety rules and regulations.
* Manages the plant’s production function while maintaining working relationships with other departments to ensure smooth operation.
* Reviews sales forecast and schedules production to ascertain and meet production quantity and quality requirements.
* Review production and operating reports, and resolve operational, manufacturing, and maintenance problems to ensure safety, while minimizing costs and preventing operational delays.
* Complies, stores, and retrieves production data. Monitors physical inventory levels.
* Oversee employee training requirements.
* Additional major functions include planning, annual budgeting and monthly forecasting, reporting of department’s effectiveness, safeguarding assets, and environmental compliance.
* This position requires knowledge equivalent to that which normally would be acquired through a bachelor’s degree in mechanical, industrial, or chemical engineering, or related field.
* Ability to analyze, troubleshoot, critically think about, and resolve problems with field equipment.
* Make sure all equipment is mechanically sound, safe, and ready to work daily.
* Oversee the daily construction activities at work site, including scheduling of workers, delivery of equipment and materials and progress of the project.
* Professionally and positively motivate and direct activities of the crew to enable the completion of work in a safe environmentally responsible and timely manner.
* Daily pre-job preparation and organization for self and crew members, including safety meetings.
* Complete and turn in all paperwork and log in a professional, legible, and timely manner.
* Manage aggregate production to ensure goals and objectives are met.
* Responsible for maintenance and repair of all mobile and stationary equipment.
* Ensures that the workforce complies with policies, procedures, and regulations to produce a productive labor climate at plant facilities.
* Assist Plant Managers and Quality Control Departments as necessary to ensure quality products, accounts & service.
* Assist in development of riverbed aggregate sites, pit operations and reclamation.
* Equipment repair and preventative maintenance
* Interact with vendors and employees.
* Maintain a high degree of customers satisfaction and employee morale through problem solving.
* Ensure a safe working environment through daily inspections and monthly safety meetings.
* Supervise 1-2 aggregate plants (both fixed and mobile)

**Qualifications**

* High School diploma or equivalent
* A minimum of 5 years’ experience in the operations of a sand and gravel pit.
* Experience in a supervisory capacity
* Knowledge of MSHA rules and regulations
* Experience in planning, design, and project management
* Minimum of two years of operating experience
* Ability to understand and follow instructions.
* Ability to learn the methods and practices used in our business.
* Ability to perform strenuous work in varying weather conditions.
* Knowledge of heavy equipment including but not limited to loaders, dozers, and hydraulic excavators and off-road haul trucks. Plant processing includes, but is not limited to water pumps, generators, electrical control components, vibratory screens, sand screws, conveyors, radial stackers, material washers, scales, settling basins, vibratory feeders, and log washers.
* Ability to meet deadlines and multi-task.

**Physical Demands & Work Environment**

Must be able to walk on uneven terrain, climb stairs and ladders, occasionally lift up to 50 pounds, wear required PPE, and work extended hours as needed. Valid driver's license and ability to safely conduct site inspections required.

**NOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES**

* Ability to understand and follow instructions.
* Ability to learn the methods and practices used in the Pits.
* Ability to perform strenuous work in varying weather conditions.

Salary: $80,000 - $105,000 DOE

Bonus Potential: 10%

* Telemedicine
* Health Advocate Service
* Dental & Orthodontics
* Vision
* 10% profit Sharing
* FSA Medical & Dependent Care
* Paid Parental Leave
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Employee Assistance Program
* Wellness Incentive Bonus Program
* Life and AD&D
* Short-Term and Long-Term Disability
* Paid Vacation
* Paid Holidays
* 401(k)

card.description:

If you're ready to be part of our legacy of hope and innovation, we encourage you to take the first step and explore our current job openings. Your best is waiting to be discovered.
 
 
Day - 08 Hour (United States of America)
 
 
**This is a Stanford Health Care job.**
**A Brief Overview**
The Director of Supply Chain Operational Excellence is a senior leadership role driving enterprise‑wide efficiency, innovation, and transformation across a Gartner top‑2 ranked healthcare supply chain. With system‑wide influence and a seat at the leadership table, this role partners closely with the Chief Supply Chain Officer and Vice President of Strategic Initiatives to turn strategy into measurable results. The ideal candidate combines healthcare supply chain expertise with strong program management skills and a passion for developing people, leading change, and delivering measurable, enterprise‑wide impact.
 
 
**Locations**
Stanford Health Care
 
 
**What You Will Do**

* Maintain continuous alignment with defined organizational and departmental strategic business objectives in conjunction with leadership.
* Direct and ensure the efficient operation of day-to-day activities of the team and ensure competency of all staff.
* Supports and partners on Change Management, Training and Communications activities as needed for effective performance improvement and project management.
* Act in an advisory capacity to all Supply Chain divisions, programs, staff and leaders.
* Provide expertise, guidance and training on Performance Improvement and Project Management best practices.
* Apply LEAN/Six Sigma principles and methods to identify waste reduction and performance optimization opportunities across Supply Chain operations.
* Implement, oversee and continuously improve Supply Chain systems, processes and standard work to drive the efficient management of operations across Logistics, Sourcing, Procurement, Business Office, Resiliency, Sustainability, Data Management and other functions.
* Build, develop and grow business relationships with Supply Chain’s key stakeholders and partners including but not limited to the Interventional Platform, A/P, Pharmacy, and IT.
* Lead cross-departmental initiatives, establishing strong governance, communication, and accountability to deliver progress measurable through mutually agreed KPIs.
* Align and collaborate with the enterprise Performance Improvement team and Stanford Operating System (SOS).
* Lead the implementation of programs and/or projects as assigned by the Administrative Director.

**Education Qualifications**

* Requires a Bachelor’s degree in a work-related discipline/field from an accredited college or university.
* Relevant experience in lieu of degree may be considered. Relevant experience in lieu of degree is in addition to the experience requirements for this position.

**Experience Qualifications**

* Seven (7) years of progressively responsible and directly related work experience.

**Required Knowledge, Skills And Abilities**

* Must have strong leadership and interpersonal skills and be effective at people management including the ability to delegate assignments and share decision-making with team members and direct reports as appropriate.
* Excellent communication skills including the ability to present, and to write in a clear and understandable manner.
* Ability to understand complex verbal or written instructions and translate to action to deliver quantitative and qualitative results.
* Must be well organized and systematic, and able to design, implement and maintain standard work processes.
* Knowledge of project management methodologies to lead complex project teams and large scope projects, including managing resources (people, costs, time).
* Familiar with and able to apply Lean Six Sigma concepts and techniques including value stream mapping, kaizen, Five Whys, VoC, RCA etc. for structured process improvement.
* Demonstrated expertise in leading change management initiatives within Agile delivery environments.
* Ability to multi-task and handle multiple priorities while managing aggressive deadlines. Knowledge of Supply Chain functions, practices, and operational challenges.
* Understanding of healthcare and clinical concepts.

**Licenses and Certifications**

* Lean Six Sigma Certification preferred .
* PMP - Project Mgmt Professional preferred .
* CMRP (Certified Materials & Resource Professionals) preferred.

**Physical Demands and Work Conditions**
**Blood Borne Pathogens**

* Category II - Tasks that involve NO exposure to blood, body fluids or tissues, but employment may require performing unplanned Category I tasks

**These Principles Apply To ALL Employees**
**SHC Commitment to Providing an Exceptional Patient & Family Experience**
*Stanford Health Care sets a high standard for delivering value and an exceptional experience for our patients and families. Candidates for employment and existing employees must adopt and execute C-I-CARE standards for all of patients, families and towards each other. C-I-CARE is the foundation of Stanford’s patient-experience and represents a framework for patient-centered interactions. Simply put, we do what it takes to enable and empower patients and families to focus on health, healing and recovery.
 
 
You will do this by executing against our three experience pillars, from the patient and family’s perspective:*

* Know Me: Anticipate my needs and status to deliver effective care
* Show Me the Way: Guide and prompt my actions to arrive at better outcomes and better health
* Coordinate for Me: Own the complexity of my care through coordination

**Equal Opportunity Employer Stanford Health Care (SHC) strongly values diversity and is committed to equal opportunity and non-discrimination in**
**all of**
**its policies and practices, including the area of employment. Accordingly, SHC does not discriminate against any person on the basis of race, color, sex, sexual orientation or gender identity and/or expression, religion, age, national or ethnic origin, political beliefs, marital status, medical condition, genetic information, veteran status, or disability, or the perception of any of the above. People of all genders, members of all racial and ethnic groups, people with disabilities, and veterans are encouraged to apply. Qualified applicants with criminal convictions will be considered after an individualized assessment of the conviction and the job requirements.**
Base Pay Scale: Generally starting at $81.59 - $108.12 per hour
 
 
The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be set based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to, internal equity, experience, education, specialty and training. This pay scale is not a promise of a particular wage.

Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

**About the Role**
------------------

The Director, Revenue Cycle Management provides strategic leadership across key Revenue Cycle functions, including outsourced operations and vendor management, credit balance management, and quality assurance. This role is accountable for improving financial and operational performance, strengthening controls, and ensuring internal teams and external partners consistently meet established service, quality, and compliance expectations.

 
 

You will partner across Revenue Cycle, Finance, Compliance, Operations, IT, and Training to improve cash and accounts receivable performance, resolve operational risks, and drive standardized, sustainable processes. This role provides leadership across multiple teams, vendors, and functional areas and translates organizational strategy into measurable operational goals and results.

 
 

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Lead Revenue Cycle operations and strategic support functions across areas such as patient access, business office operations, claims, accounts receivable, registration, insurance verification, payment and adjustment activities, and customer service.
* Provide governance and performance oversight for **third-party and BPO vendors**, including service-level agreements (SLAs), key performance indicators (KPIs), productivity, quality, contractual performance, issue escalation, and remediation.
* Lead **credit balance operations**, including identification, validation, refunds, adjustments, aging, resolution, root-cause analysis, and prevention of recurring patient and payer credit balances.
* Lead the **Revenue Cycle Quality Assurance program**, including quality standards, audit methodologies, sampling, scoring, performance reporting, corrective action plans, controls, and ongoing monitoring.
* Drive financial and operational performance across assigned Revenue Cycle functions, including cash, accounts receivable, operating expense, vendor spend, quality, compliance, customer experience, and productivity.
* Partner with Revenue Cycle, Finance, Compliance, Operations, IT, Training, and external vendors to identify operational risks, resolve complex issues, standardize processes, and execute continuous improvement initiatives.
* Establish governance, reporting, and escalation processes that identify performance gaps and support accountability, risk mitigation, root-cause analysis, and measurable improvement.

*Other duties may be assigned as needed to meet Company goals.*

 
 

**Basic Requirements**
----------------------

* **Degree or equivalent experience. Typically requires 12+ years of professional experience and 4+ years of management experience.**
* Demonstrated professional experience in **Revenue Cycle Management or Revenue Cycle Operations**, including accounts receivable or related healthcare financial operations.
* Experience leading **third-party vendors, outsourced operations, or Business Process Outsourcing (BPO)** relationships, including vendor performance, SLAs, KPIs, or contract performance.
* Experience with **credit balance management**, including refunds, adjustments, resolution, aging, or related accounts receivable processes.
* Experience with **Revenue Cycle quality assurance, auditing, controls, or performance improvement**.
* Experience leading cross-functional teams and initiatives across complex or multi-site healthcare operations.
 

 

**Preferred Skills/Experience**
-------------------------------

* Experience leading Revenue Cycle functions across hospital, physician, infusion, or other healthcare environments.
* Demonstrated experience with root-cause analysis, process standardization, continuous improvement, risk mitigation, and corrective action planning.
* Strong ability to influence internal stakeholders and external partners and translate complex operational and financial information into actionable business decisions.

If located in DFW area, the selected candidate may be expected to work on‑site at our Las Colinas office a minimum of two (2) days per week, with the remaining days worked remotely. Specific in‑office days may be designated according to team needs and business priorities.

card.description:
**Position Summary**
--------------------

The Director, Quality is responsible for leading multiple manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality resources in the execution of the overall STERIS Quality System. This position is principally responsible for manufacturing/service site or functional quality system execution to drive product/service quality improvement and ensure compliance with, as appropriate, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, MDSAP, FDA QMSR CFR Part 820/211, EU MDR, and other applicable standards. Supporting the GI Reprocessing business, this role provides quality leadership for products, processes, and services that help healthcare providers safely clean, disinfect, and reprocess gastrointestinal endoscopes and related equipment. The Director will champion a culture of quality, compliance, and continuous improvement, helping ensure the delivery of safe, effective, and reliable solutions that support infection prevention, patient safety, and customer confidence. The Quality Director will lead teams of quality managers and engineers responsible for product and service quality, supplier quality, new product/service support, continuous improvement initiatives, and quality system execution. This leader will partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, and Commercial teams to drive operational excellence, mitigate risk, support innovation, and enhance quality performance across the GI Reprocessing portfolio.

Preferred onsite location: Mentor, OH, with consideration for candidates based in Plymouth, MN or Conroe, TX.

**What You’ll do as a Director Quality**
----------------------------------------

* The Director, Quality will have responsibility for the following: Leads manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality staff in the execution and continuous improvement of the STERIS Quality System. Operates with a focus on the following objectives:
 + Ensures site level compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
 + Drives strategies and methods to continuously improve capital, consumable and service product quality performance.
 + Establishes clear and consistent quality measurement systems in order to monitor and drive results.
 + Leads quality planning and the execution of assigned New Product/Service Development (NPD) projects to achieve targeted quality deliverable adherence.
 + Drives targeted supplier quality improvement efforts and oversees supplier evaluation, approval, and control for assigned manufacturing sites.
 + Assists in the continuous improvement and standardization of quality system procedures and monitor effectiveness.
 + Supports the reliability function by integrating design for reliability tools and techniques within the local projects.
 + Leads quality planning efforts through cross-functional teaming at a site level.
* Supports the New Product/Service Development process and projects to ensure projects attain cost, quality, and delivery objectives.
* Directs local staff on planning sequential and concurrent quality activities. Establish planning and monitoring tools and techniques.
* Provides Quality viewpoints and opinions in planning and specifying existing and future products.
* Assists in the development of the Quality budget. Helps to ensures resources are adequate to fully support the Quality System.
* Takes ownership of all local quality issues, projects, and development activities. Works closely with the site’s Senior Management Teams to provide strategic direction and development of the manufacturing sites product quality strategies and tactics.
* Manages and provide direction to a teams of quality professionals both at corporate and manufacturing sites, with responsibility for hiring, performance management, appropriate staffing, and deployment of resources.
* Assures that local sites maintain and improve operational and quality systems to remain in a state of compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
* Works closely with the regulatory function to ensure compliance to appropriate ISO and FDA standards; plans for and assists in the management of external audits.
* Leads manufacturing and service site quality teams to ensure alignment to operations, support of Lean efforts and drive quality improvement performance for products, services, and processes across the sites.
* This individual has autonomy to perform the duties of Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance (PRRC) on behalf of STERIS legal manufacturing entities under the EU MDR. This individual shall suffer no disadvantage within the organization in relation to proper fulfilment of his or her duties in lieu of article 15 of the EU MDR.

**The Experience, Skills, and Abilities Needed**
------------------------------------------------

**Required:**

* Bachelor’s Degree (Engineering or related technical field)
* Minimum 10 years of experience with increased responsibility leading quality system and product quality improvement efforts. Exceptional leadership manifested through organizing and motivating teams toward their respective goals by employing hands-on management.
* Must fulfil the experience requirements listed in Article 15 of the EUMDR (PRRC).
* A solid quality foundation indicated by a demonstrated understanding of Lean/Six Sigma, quality system, and product/process improvement methodologies.
* Solid business acumen and proven ability to build and lead process and product improvement strategies and results.
* Strong expertise in analytical methods, quality systems, and continuous improvement methods.
* Excellent interpersonal, as well as verbal and written communication skills in order to develop and maintain rapport and effective internal and external relationships to support business success.
* The ability to work hard and deliver results under pressure, as well as the willingness to address and shift priorities in rapidly changing markets.

**Preferred:**

* Advanced degree.
* Experience with statistical analysis software and Visio.
* Experience in medical device industry.

**Other:**

* Excellent problem-solving skills.
* Focus on identification of potential issues and continuous improvement.
* Experience working on cross-functional teams and on own initiative.
* Demonstrated excellent organizational, oral, and written communications skills.
* Must have PC experience, as well as working familiarity of desktop applications including Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

**What STERIS Offers**
----------------------

We value our employees and are committed to providing a comprehensive benefits package that supports your health, well-being, and financial future.

Here is a brief overview of what we offer:

 

* Market competitive pay
* Extensive paid time off and (9) added holidays
* Excellent healthcare, dental, and vision benefits
* Long/short term disability coverage
* 401(K) with company match
* Maternity and parental leave
* Additional add on benefits/discounts for programs such as pet insurance
* Tuition reimbursement and continued educational programs
* Excellent opportunities for advancement in a stable long-term career

card.title: Director, Quality Compliance (Hybrid - Acton, MA)
card.description:
Job Summary

The Director of Compliance provides strategic and operational leadership for critical compliance activities across the medical device organization. This role leads regulatory inspection readiness, product issue escalation and compliance risk assessment, regulatory agency responses, correction and removal activities, and large-scale compliance improvement initiatives.
 
 
The Director serves as a senior compliance partner to Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Safety, Operations, R&D, Supply Chain, and business leadership, ensuring significant quality and compliance issues are rapidly assessed, appropriately escalated, and effectively resolved. The position requires strong judgment, executive communication, and the ability to lead complex, cross-functional activities in a highly regulated environment.
 
 
Beyond compliance subject-matter leadership, the Director owns the compliance function's budget and resourcing, shapes its organizational strategy and structure, and contributes to broader business planning — balancing business objectives with compliance risk and representing the function in strategic and operational business reviews. The Director leads a global team of regional compliance specialists, building organizational capability across all manufacturing sites and functions.



**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

Organizational Strategy & Business Leadership

* Shape the multi-year strategy and organizational design for the compliance function, including workforce planning, capability building, and succession planning.

* Lead, develop, and manage a global team of compliance professionals, including direct oversight of regional compliance specialists across manufacturing sites.

* Partner with business, Quality, and Regulatory leadership to align compliance priorities with broader business strategy, product roadmaps, and operational plans.

* Represent the compliance organization in business planning, budget reviews, and strategic planning forums, providing a compliance-risk perspective to business decisions.

* Build organizational capability and structure to scale the compliance function as the business grows.

Inspection Readiness

* Establish and maintain an enterprise inspection-readiness program supporting regulatory inspections and other external assessments.

* Lead inspection preparation, including readiness assessments, mock inspections, documentation reviews, front-room/back-room preparation, subject-matter-expert coaching, and inspection logistics.

* Identify systemic readiness gaps and drive corrective actions to improve sustained inspection preparedness.

* Develop inspection-readiness metrics, lessons learned, and continuous-improvement mechanisms.

Product Issue Escalation & Risk Assessment

* Lead or facilitate cross-functional assessments of significant product quality, safety, compliance, and regulatory issues requiring senior-level escalation.

* Ensure emerging product issues are evaluated using structured, documented risk-based decision-making.

* Partner with Medical Safety, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Engineering, Operations, and other functions to evaluate product and compliance risk and determine appropriate escalation and response.

* Provide independent compliance challenge and guidance when significant product-related decisions could create regulatory or patient-safety implications.

* Ensure escalated issues have clear ownership, documented rationale, timely decisions, and appropriate executive visibility.

Regulatory Agency Responses

* Lead the development and coordination of responses to regulatory inspection observations, agency inquiries, compliance correspondence, and other significant regulatory matters.

* Establish cross-functional response teams, governance, deliverables, and escalation mechanisms.

* Ensure responses are factually supported, internally consistent, appropriately reviewed, and supported by sustainable corrective actions.

* Monitor commitments made to regulatory authorities through completion and verify appropriate evidence of implementation and effectiveness.

* Provide senior leadership with clear assessments of response status, risks, dependencies, and potential compliance exposure.

Correction & Removal Oversight and Execution

* Provide oversight and leadership for product corrections and removals, including recalls and field actions, in partnership with Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Safety, Supply Chain, Commercial, and other relevant functions.

* Lead governance and execution for complex or high-risk correction and removal activities.

* Ensure decisions are supported by appropriate health-hazard, quality, regulatory, and compliance risk assessments.

* Establish clear accountability for affected-product identification, communications, execution, reconciliation, effectiveness monitoring, and closure.

* Monitor significant field actions through completion and escalate implementation risks or unexpected trends to senior leadership.

* Drive lessons learned and systemic improvements following significant product actions.

Large-Scale Compliance Improvement Projects

* Lead enterprise or multi-site compliance remediation and improvement programs involving significant regulatory, quality-system, or business risk.

* Translate regulatory observations, internal audit findings, systemic quality issues, or emerging compliance risks into structured remediation strategies and executable workstreams.

* Establish program governance, accountability, milestones, risk management, escalation processes, and executive reporting.

* Coordinate activities across functions and sites to ensure remediation addresses underlying systemic issues rather than isolated symptoms.

* Evaluate implementation progress and evidence of effectiveness to support sustainable closure.

* Serve as a compliance leader for major transformation initiatives involving quality-system processes, governance, controls, or organizational capabilities.

Leadership & Governance Responsibilities

* Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership on significant compliance and regulatory risks.

* Provide independent compliance perspective during complex or high-risk decision-making.

* Establish governance mechanisms that enable timely escalation, transparent risk communication, and clear accountability.

* Develop organizational capability in inspection readiness, regulatory response, issue escalation, and compliance risk management.

* Promote a culture of proactive risk identification, regulatory accountability, patient safety, and sustainable compliance.

* Mentor and develop compliance professionals and cross-functional leaders involved in regulatory and remediation activities.

* Partner with business leadership on budget planning and resource allocation decisions affecting the compliance organization.

 

**Qualifications Required**
---------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, life sciences, quality, regulatory affairs, or a related discipline and 12+ years’ industry experience.

* Significant progressive experience in Quality, Compliance, Regulatory Affairs, or related functions within the medical device or similarly regulated life-sciences industry.

* Demonstrated experience supporting or leading regulatory inspections and inspection readiness.

* Experience managing significant product quality or compliance escalations and structured risk assessments.

* Experience developing or coordinating responses to regulatory authorities.

* Strong working knowledge of medical-device quality-system and post-market regulatory requirements.

* Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional compliance or remediation programs.

* Experience managing budgets, resource planning, or organizational design within a compliance, quality, or regulatory function.

* Demonstrated business acumen, with the ability to balance business objectives and compliance risk in decision-making.

* Prior people leadership experience, including managing geographically distributed teams, strongly preferred.

* Strong executive communication, judgment, influence, and problem-solving skills.

 

**Core Competencies**
---------------------

* Regulatory and compliance strategy

* Organizational strategy and workforce planning

* Budget and resource management

* Business acumen and strategic planning

* Inspection management and readiness

* Product and compliance risk assessment

* Regulatory agency communication

* Correction and removal governance

* Quality-system remediation

* Program and project leadership

* Executive-level communication

* Cross-functional influence

* Critical decision-making under pressure

* Root-cause and systemic problem solving

* Change leadership

Additional Information:



Compensation & Benefits:

For U.S.-based positions only, the annual base salary range for this role is $172,400.00 - $258,575.00

This position may also be eligible for incentive compensation.

We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:
• Medical, dental, and vision insurance
• 401(k) with company match
• Paid time off (PTO)
• And additional employee wellness programs

Application Details:
This job posting will remain open until the position is filled.
To apply, please visit the Insulet Careers site and submit your application online.

Actual pay depends on skills, experience, and education.

Insulet Corporation (NASDAQ: PODD), headquartered in Massachusetts, is an innovative medical device company dedicated to simplifying life for people with diabetes and other conditions through its Omnipod product platform. The Omnipod Insulin Management System provides a unique alternative to traditional insulin delivery methods. With its simple, wearable design, the tubeless disposable Pod provides up to three days of non-stop insulin delivery, without the need to see or handle a needle. Insulet’s flagship innovation, the Omnipod 5 Automated Insulin Delivery System, integrates with a continuous glucose monitor to manage blood sugar with no multiple daily injections, zero fingersticks, and can be controlled by a compatible personal smartphone in the U.S. or by the Omnipod 5 Controller. Insulet also leverages the unique design of its Pod by tailoring its Omnipod technology platform for the delivery of non-insulin subcutaneous drugs across other therapeutic areas. For more information, please visit insulet.com and omnipod.com.
 
 
We are looking for highly motivated, performance-driven individuals to be a part of our expanding team. We do this by hiring amazing people guided by shared values who exceed customer expectations. Our continued success depends on it!

At Insulet Corporation all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

card.description:
Responsibilities:

The Director, Compliance, Quality & Risk Management provides enterprise-wide strategic and operational leadership for the Foundation’s compliance, organizational quality, and enterprise risk management functions. 
The Director is accountable for establishing and maintaining integrated frameworks, governance processes, and performance standards that strengthen organizational accountability, regulatory compliance, operational effectiveness, and proactive risk management across Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation. The Director owns the enterprise risk management framework, leads enterprise quality improvement and compliance oversight, and partners with executive and operational leaders to identify systemic risks, establish organizational standards, and drive measurable improvements. The Director provides leadership across a complex, multi-state healthcare organization, translating regulatory requirements, organizational risks, and performance insights into actionable strategies that advance the Foundation’s mission, operational integrity, and long-term sustainability.
 
 
This role strengthens Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation’s ability to manage regulatory complexity, maintain consistent quality standards, identify enterprise risks, and provide coordinated oversight across a geographically dispersed organization. Through integrated governance and disciplined execution, the Director helps protect the Foundation’s mission, supports organizational sustainability, and advances the delivery of safe, ethical, high-quality services.

* Enterprise Compliance Leadership
* Quality Management and Continuous Improvement
* Enterprise Risk Management and Patient Safety
* Leadership, Governance and Enterprise Integration

Qualifications:

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business administration, nursing, public health, compliance, risk management, law, or a related field.
* Seven or more years of progressive experience in healthcare compliance, quality management, risk management, patient safety, or related disciplines.
* Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
* Three or more years of experience leading teams, programs, or significant cross-functional initiatives.
* Experience managing complex projects and collaborating with executive and operational leaders.
* Demonstrated knowledge of healthcare regulatory frameworks, compliance practices, and quality improvement methodologies.
* Strong analytical, communication, investigation, and problem-solving capabilities.
* Demonstrated sound judgment, professional integrity, and ability to handle sensitive or confidential matters.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Advanced degree in healthcare administration, business administration, public health, law, or a related field.
* Experience in behavioral healthcare, substance use disorder treatment, or a multi-state healthcare organization.
* Experience with Joint Commission or other applicable accreditation standards.
* Knowledge of HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, CMS requirements, and state behavioral health regulations.
* Professional certification such as CHC, CHPC, CPHQ, CPHRM, or equivalent.
* Experience designing enterprise risk frameworks, compliance programs, or integrated quality systems.
* Experience leading organizational transformation or consolidating multiple functions

Overview:

The Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation is the largest nonprofit addiction recovery organization in the United States. It is also one of the most mission-driven places you will find. The Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation team is passionate about providing hope and ultimately healing. As a living, growing and evolving institution, the Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation is – at our core- a people-powered organization. Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation is comprised of 1600+ employees, seventeen treatment sites and produces $190 million dollars in annual revenue. This exemplary organization serves nearly 25,000 people annually and is committed to provide hope and healing for those experiencing addiction to alcohol and other drugs.

What makes this organization unique is its total ecosystem approach to prevention, education, research, advocacy and treatment. All of the parts of the organization work together to inform, develop and deliver evidence- based practices that help people reclaim their futures and restore their hope.

Being “a best place to work” is a strategic goal of Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation and it’s a goal that every employee plays an active role in helping to achieve. Our culture is a reflection of how encouraged and energized we each feel about contributing our ideas and performing to our greatest ability. Join us and do meaningful work.

We deeply value our employees. Working at Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation includes a comprehensive benefits package, including:

* Competitive Health, Dental and Vision Plans
* Retirement savings plan with employer match
* Paid time-off
* Tuition reimbursement

The Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation is proud to be an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. We believe that diversity and inclusion among our colleagues is critical to our success as a force of healing and hope for individuals, families and communities affected by addiction to alcohol and other drugs; and we seek to recruit, develop and retain the most talented people from a diverse candidate pool.

card.description:
Description:

**The Company:**

This publicly held clinical-stage biotechnology company is focused on developing treatments for patients suffering from complex rare diseases using its novel cell penetrating peptide technology platform. Their lead product candidate, nomlabofusp, is a subcutaneously administered, recombinant fusion protein intended to deliver human frataxin (FXN), an essential protein to the mitochondria of patients with Friedreich’s ataxia. Friedreich’s ataxia is a rare, progressive, and fatal disease in which patients are unable to produce sufficient FXN due to a genetic abnormality.

The company has 80 employees and has assembled an experienced management team, each of whom has over 20 years of pharmaceutical industry experience. The management team, employees, and consultants have significant expertise in discovery, nonclinical and clinical development, regulatory affairs, commercialization, and the development of manufacturing processes utilizing good manufacturing practices (GMPs).

The company’s strategy is to become a leader in the treatment of rare diseases by leveraging their technology platform and applying their team’s know-how and expertise to the development of CTI-1601 and other future pipeline programs. They are best characterized by entrepreneurial and scientific leadership and a participatory workforce committed to success.

**Position Summary:**

The Director, GxP Vendor Management is responsible for leading Larimar’s GxP vendor management and audit programs and collaborating with key functional area stakeholders to ensure vendors are selected, qualified, managed and overseen in compliance with Larimar and regulatory requirements. This role owns the full vendor lifecycle and will shape the program’s strategy as Larimar seeks BLA approval, progresses with Phase 3 trial and plans for commercialization.

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Lead and implement the strategic direction of the vendor management and audit programs at Larimar.
* Own the risk-based vendor qualification framework, including risk tiering and minimum oversight expectations for each tier, and manage day-to-day qualification activities through vendor audit and assessment, qualification, approval and filing of vendor-related qualification documentation.
* Maintain an approved vendor list and a master tracker of all GxP vendors (current, historic, and planned) as the single source of truth for vendor qualification/requalification, audit, and Quality Agreements.
* Partner with functional areas to develop and oversee execution of the risk-based annual external audit plan, including auditor assignments, audit tracking, follow up of audit responses and CAPAs, and filing of audit documentation.
* Manage the internal audit program including development and execution of internal audit plan to adequately assess Larimar’s internal processes.
* Manage the Quality Agreement program, including development and maintenance of Quality Agreements, and partner with Legal and functional areas to ensure Quality Agreements are in place and current with applicable vendors.
* Partner with functional areas to develop, review and maintain risk-based vendor oversight plans, including expectations for KPIs; governance meetings; issue escalation; oversight activities, frequency, responsibility, and documentation requirements; and verification that vendors and their subcontractors use qualified personnel.
* Conduct training on vendor management and audit programs to ensure functional areas understand and appropriately execute their responsibilities.
* Partner with functional areas to identify vendor deviations to assess issues potentially impacting the vendor qualification status or required oversight.
* Develop Vendor Management metrics, analyze vendor performance and compliance trends, and lead a periodic cross-functional vendor review that feeds into Quality Management Review.
* Ensure inspection readiness in the vendor management function and assist functional areas with readiness related to selection, qualification, management and oversight of their vendors.
* Evaluate and implement electronic vendor management systems, as applicable.

Requirements:

**Qualifications:**

* BS/BA in a life science or related field, or equivalent industry experience.
* 10+ years’ experience in the Pharmaceutical/Biotechnology industry, including at least 5 years leading vendor management/audit programs in a GxP environment.
* Expert knowledge of FDA, EMA, MHRA and ICH GxP regulations and guidelines, including ICH E6(R3) expectations for sponsor oversight of service providers.
* Strong GxP foundation associated with vendor oversight.
* Demonstrated experience planning and managing GxP vendor and internal audits, including follow up of audit responses and CAPAs.
* Experience developing and negotiating Quality Agreements with CROs, laboratories and other GxP service providers.
* Proficient with Veeva Systems, including Veeva Vault QualityDocs, desirable.
* Experience applying risk-based approaches to vendor tiering and oversight.
* Strong communication skills with all levels of the organization and external vendors, and the ability to influence functional areas without direct authority.
* Excellent organizational skills, analytical and problem-solving abilities, and strong verbal and writing skills.

**Benefits:**

Larimar Therapeutics offers all employees incentive stock options, a comprehensive benefits plan including 401K, and a flexible PTO policy.

***Equal Opportunity Employment***

*We are committed to equal-employment principles, and we recognize the value of committed employees who feel they are being treated in an equitable and professional manner. We strive to find ways to attract, develop and retain the talent needed to meet business objectives, and to recruit and employ highly qualified individuals representing the diverse communities in which we live.*

*Employment policies and decisions on employment and promotion are based on merit, qualifications, performance, and business needs. The decisions and criteria governing the employment relationship with all employees are made in a non-discriminatory manner—without regard to age, race, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth or medical condition related to pregnancy or childbirth), gender identity or expression, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, legally protected genetic information, marital status, veteran status, military status, sexual orientation, or any other factor determined to be an unlawful basis for such decisions by federal, state, or local statutes.*

Duties Description Kirby Forensic Psychiatric Center (KFPC), an Office of Mental Health (OMH) secure forensic facility, is recruiting a Deputy Director, Psychiatric Center 1 - Quality Management (DDPC 1 - QM) to oversee their Quality Management Program.
 
 
The DDPC 1 - QM is an essential member of the facility's Executive Management Team. Under the general direction of the Executive Director and in close collaboration with the facility leadership team at KFPC, the DDPC 1 – QM participates in developing, implementing, interpreting, and evaluating the facility's mission, goals, and policies and how they impact the care and clinical treatment provided to the adults, youth, and families they serve.
 
 
The DDPC 1 – QM is responsible for:
 

* Supervising all departments assigned to the Quality Management Program - program evaluation, risk management, utilization review, health information management, and staff development.
* Ensuring compliance with OMH, The Joint Commission (TJC), the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), and external regulatory agencies standards, cultural competence, and continuous quality improvement.
* Ensuring high-quality and effective care in both inpatient and outpatient programs.

Minimum Qualifications Minimum Qualifications:
 
 
A. Education
 
 
A master’s degree in a mental hygiene discipline, hospital or health administration, or other administrative area specifically related to health care, sociology, statistics, or quantitative research; or a license to practice medicine in New York State or Canada.
 
 
AND
 
 
B. Experience
 
 
Six (6) years of experience in a mental health program or health care setting that includes one of the following:
 
 
1. Four (4) years of managerial experience in one quality management component area, such as program evaluation, clinical risk management, standards compliance, survey readiness, utilization review, or a closely related area; or
 
2. Three (3) years of managerial experience in two of the above quality management component areas; or
 
3. Two (2) years of managerial experience in three of the above quality management component areas.

Additional Comments About KFPC
 
KFPC, located on Ward’s Island in New York City, provides inpatient treatment and rehabilitation to pretrial defendants who were deemed unfit to stand trial and were court ordered for restoration of fitness to stand trial and individuals who have been found not guilty by reason of insanity.
 
 
KFPC is committed to supporting underserved individuals and delivering treatment with respect for each individual's privacy and rights along with activities and initiatives to reduce disparities in access, quality, and treatment for underserved populations.
 
 
About OMH
 
OMH operates the largest state mental health system in the country, with 23 hospitals, 90 clinics, two world-class research institutes, a secure residential center, and a network of community services. OMH hospitals are all Joint Commission-accredited and recognized as among the best mental health hospital systems in the United States. OMH believes everyone should have an equal opportunity to achieve mental wellness. This means implementing services and policies to reduce disparities in access, quality, and treatment outcomes for historically marginalized, underserved, and unserved populations.
 
 
If you would like to join KFPC and contribute to a workforce dedicated to public service, we offer:
 

* Generous paid time off, including thirteen (13) vacation days, eight (8) sick days, and five (5) personal days accrued during the first year of employment; thirteen (13) paid holidays each year.
* Option to choose a NYS health insurance plan that meets your needs.
* Dental and vision coverage.
* Enrollment in the New York State and Local Retirement System (NYSLRS) or a voluntary defined contribution plan.

 
The posted salary includes the Downstate Adjustment of $4,150.
 
 
#LI-DNI

card.description:
**Role Description**
The Vice President of Quality Assurance is a senior, full-time remote role responsible for leading the quality vision, strategy, and execution across Allianz Trade’s operations. This position oversees the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of quality assurance frameworks, policies, and procedures to ensure consistent service delivery and compliance with internal standards and external regulations. Day-to-day tasks include directing quality audits, monitoring quality performance metrics, identifying root causes of issues, and driving corrective and preventive actions in partnership with cross-functional leaders. The role involves collaborating with operations, technology, compliance, and risk management teams to embed quality best practices into processes, systems, and customer interactions. The Vice President will also guide and mentor quality teams, manage departmental budgets, and report on quality objectives, outcomes, and strategic initiatives to executive leadership.

**Qualifications**

* Strong background in Quality Assurance and Quality Control, with demonstrated experience designing and leading enterprise-wide quality programs.
* Expertise in Quality Management and Quality Auditing, including setting performance standards, conducting audits, and implementing continuous improvement initiatives.
* Solid understanding of Regulatory Requirements relevant to financial services or insurance, with the ability to translate regulatory expectations into practical quality controls.
* Proven leadership experience in senior quality or operational roles, including managing teams, influencing stakeholders, and driving change across complex organizations.
* Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with proficiency in using data and metrics to evaluate performance and prioritize improvements.
* Strong communication and collaboration abilities, including presenting to executive audiences and partnering effectively with global and cross-functional teams in a remote environment.
* Relevant academic background, such as a bachelor’s or master’s degree in business, operations, engineering, quality management, or a related field; professional certifications (e.g., Six Sigma, ISO, CQE/CQA) are a plus.
* Experience within insurance, financial services, or risk management industries is highly beneficial, along with familiarity with digital tools and enterprise quality systems.
